findings.summary: Reassessed against the repaired bytes: removing qualifier.all.environment broadens retrieval to absent or different environment cues, including a different parser or Python version. It does not establish support there. The unchanged rule names Python csv.reader and these inputs, while gate_rationale, gate_evidence and evidence_summary explicitly preserve the Python 3.11.6 supplied-sample boundary. Because those limits accompany retrieval, this broader discovery behavior does not by itself establish a semantic blocker; the reviewer must explicitly disposition it and must not describe environment filtering as retained.

The repeated local observation again fires revision 1's falsifier on A3: literal splitting gives 4 pieces and csv.reader gives 3 fields. Every supplied row gives 3 parser fields. A4 count agreement and the old unquoted rows do not establish generic escaping correctness, malformed-input validation, dialect coverage or cross-context transfer. The repaired proposal retains its scoped field-count claim and original counterevidence without introducing those unsupported extensions.

The sole semantic JSON change is qualifier.all.environment from [python 3 stdlib csv] to []. Against unchanged actual task cues, the documented retrieval predicate rejects the original candidate and accepts the repaired candidate. Missing domain, missing operation or a different artifact still rejects the repaired candidate. This resolves the previous actual-cue predicate defect in the frozen artifact; actual revision-2 store retrieval remains a coordinator-owned check and was not performed in this pass.
